messages.author: 28f7cf43544f2467
messages.subject: Specify Tick Labels
parts:
I would like to change the tick labels displayed on the y-axis.

For example...I would like to override the existing tick labels on the
y-axis with the sequence of letters from P to A (bottom to top)
instead of the default of numbers from 1 to 16 (bottom to top).

I have tried creating a set of characters and referencing the list of
characters in the scale_y_continuous parameter as follows...but get a
"non-continuous variable supplied to scale_y_continuous" error.

labels = rev(LETTERS[1:16])

Any help is greatly appreciated.

messages.author: 599a13812d4cd3e8
messages.subject: Re: Specify Tick Labels
parts:
(notes lack of reproducible example ...)

Sounds like your Y axis is being interpreted as continuous (which would be the case for numbers). Sounds like what you want is a y axis which is an (ordered) factor, P to A (is that 16 letters?)?

Easiest thing to do would be to add a new column to your data frame for this factor, then plot with that on the Y axis. ggplot2 will then "do the right thing".

But a full example would make answering easier.

--J

messages.author: 14b60f9dd8872281
messages.subject: Re: Specify Tick Labels
parts:
You don't really provide enough information in your question about the
data, but assuming the data is continuous, this worked to relabel the
y axis:

df <- data.frame(x = seq(1,100), y= rnorm(100, mean=50, sd=25))
p <- ggplot(df, aes(x=x, y=y)) + geom_line()
p <- p + scale_y_continuous(breaks=seq(10,100,by=10), labels=rev
(LETTERS[1:10]), limits = c(0,100))
print(p)

messages.subject: Re: Specify Tick Labels
parts:
My full example is below. I have attached the data.frame i am working
with here (http://groups.google.com/group/ggplot2/web/results2.txt).

I produce a heat map of results for a 16x24 micro titer plate using
the above data.frame using the following code:

p = ggplot(results2,aes(SynWell_column, SynWell_row))
p + geom_tile(aes(fill=totalODdna),colour="white") +
scale_fill_gradient(low="white",high="steelblue") +
labs(x="Column",y="Row") +
scale_x_continuous(breaks=1:24) +
opts(title=paste("Yield Map"))

This poses a problem:
The view of the plate is plotted in the wrong orientation. The view
seems to be flipped 180 degrees so that well A1 is in the lower left
corner (instead of the upper left hand corner like holding the plate
in your hand and looking at it).

I can correctly display the data by using the following code:

p = ggplot(results2,aes(SynWell_column, sort
(SynWell_row,decreasing=TRUE)))
p + geom_tile(aes(fill=totalODdna),colour="white") +
scale_fill_gradient(low="white",high="steelblue") +
labs(x="Column",y="Row") +
scale_x_continuous(breaks=1:24) +
opts(title=paste("Yield Map"))

This displays the data in the logical format (A1 in the top left
corner)...but leaves the y-axis sorted the same way.

I'd like to have this sorted properly or be able to override the
labeling of the axis so that it will at least be displayed correctly.
Everything i have tried does not seem to work.

Thanks in advance for your advice!

messages.author: 599a13812d4cd3e8
messages.subject: Re: Specify Tick Labels
parts:
If I'm following you right, perhaps this works?

results2 <- read.table("~/Desktop/results2.txt")

# change the row into a factor. ggplot2 uses the order specified in the levels param to order categorical axis
results2$SynWell_row <- factor(results2$SynWell_row, levels=sort(LETTERS[1:16],decreasing=T))

# draw it
ggplot(results2,aes(SynWell_column, SynWell_row)) + geom_tile(aes(fill=totalODdna),colour="white") +

Now we have A1 in the top left, P1 on the bottom left and the axis appropriately labeled.

Does that work?

--J
